title: Surface Finish
text:
Use pre-molded expansion joint fillers for transverse expansion joints as 
detailed and shown in plans. 
560.1.9.2 Surface Finish 
Use proper tools for pavement finishing. 
560.1.9.3 Curing and Protection  
Immediately after the finishing operations, exposed concrete surfaces shall be cured 
by one of the following methods as the Contractor may elect: 
1) 
Mat Method: The entire exposed surface 
2) 
Surface shall be covered with two or more layers of burlap.  Mats shall overlap 
each other at least 150mm. The mat shall be thoroughly wetted with water prior 
to placing on concrete surface and shall be kept continuously in a saturated 
condition and in an intimate contact with concrete for not less than 7 days. 
3) 
Impervious Sheeting Method: The entire exposed surface shall be wetted with 
a fine spray of water and then covered with impervious sheeting material. 
Sheets shall be laid directly to the concrete surface with the light-colored side 
up and overlapped 12 inches when a continuous sheet is not used. The curing 
medium shall not be less than 450mm wider than the concrete surface to be 
cured and shall be secured weighted down by heavy wood planks or by placing 
a bank of moist earth along edges and laps in the sheets. Sheets shall be 
satisfactory repaired or replaced if torn or otherwise damaged during curing. 
The curing method shall remain on the concrete surface to be cured for not less 
than 7 days.  
4) 
Membrane-Curing Method: The entire exposed surface shall be covered with a 
membrane-forming curing compound.  Where Type 1 curing compound is used, 
concrete surface shall be shaded from direct rays of the sun for a period of 3 
days immediately after spraying. Curing compound shall be applied in two 
coats by hand-operated pressure sprayers at coverage of approximately 200 
square feet per gallon for both coats. The second coat shall be applied in a 
direction approximately at right angles to the direction of application of the 
first coat. Apply an additional coat to all surfaces showing discontinuity, 
pinholes or other defects. Concrete surfaces that are subjected to heavy rainfall 
within 3 hours after curing compound has been applied shall b

e re-sprayed by 
the same method stated above at no additional cost to the Employer. 
5) 
Expansion joint openings shall be sealed at the top by inserting moistened paper 
or fiber rope, or by covering with strips of waterproof paper prior to the 
application of the curing compound, in a manner to prevent the curing 
compound entering the joint. These surfaces should be adequately protected for 
7 days from pedestrian and vehicular traffic and any area damaged by 
subsequent construction within the 7-day during period shall be re-sprayed at 
no additional cost to the Employer.

563.5.2

1)

pruned to reduce the crown, pruning shall also be carried out for reasons of 
safety or to improve the health of trees. 
2) 
The Contractor shall nominate branches to be removed. Following approval by 
the Engineer, the approved branches shall be trimmed as specified. 
563.5.3 
Equipment 
All tools should be appropriate for the Work to be carried out and shall be surface 
sterilized with ethylated spirits after use on trees which are known or suspected to be 
diseased. 
563.5.4 
Appearance 
The general description of the Work to be done is to be interpreted in relation to the 
shape, size, character and condition of each individual tree.  
All operations shall be carried out so as to leave a well-balanced tree of natural shape 
to the satisfaction of the Engineer. 
563.5.5 
Inspection 
The estimate of work needed will normally have been based on judgment made from 
ground level. The Contractor shall make a careful inspection of each tree during the 
course of his work and shall report any additional defects or weaknesses which may 
be revealed.  
563.5.6 
Removal of Branches 
All final cuts shall be made into living wood to allow healing by the growth tissue.  
Cuts shall be made in such a manner as to prevent the formation of moisture holding 
pockets.  
All final cuts to be made into living wood immediately above the "branch bark ridge". 
All vertical or near vertical branches shall be cut off neatly just above the nearest 
suitable live growth. The branch shall be sawn off at an angle no greater than is 
necessary to ensure rapid shedding of water.  
Large cuts must be carefully pared to give a clean and smooth surface which will 
allow rapid healing.

text:

563.5.8 
Removal of Dead Wood from the Crown 
The Contractor shall remove all dead, diseased and dying branch wood, and broken 
stumps, throughout the crown. Final cuts to be made into living wood where possible. 
563.5.9 
Crown Thinning 
The density of the crown is to be reduced as directed by the Engineer by the cutting 
back of branches from the inner section of the crown, so as to leave the tree with a 
natural and well-balanced shape. 
563.5.10 Crown Lifting 
Limbs or small branches shall be removed as directed by the Engineer. 
563.5.11 Cavity Filling: Water Pockets in Forks  
Water pockets in forks shall be thoroughly cleaned, dried and filled with non-ridged 
filler to be approved by the Engineer; the top of the filling being sloped to give a 
rapid run-off for moisture. Where it is impossible to reach the bottom of narrow water 
pockets they may be tapped with an auger, the water drained away and the auger hole 
plugged with a hardwood level dipped in wound dressing.  
563.5.12 Digging and Transportation Procedures  
1)  
The excavated root ball size shall follow the guidelines hereafter described.  
However, each Palm, Tree, Bamboo and other Plants specimen shall be 
examined prior to transplanting by the qualified Horticulturalist and the 
Engineer and amendments made to these guidelines as dictated by the nature 
of each specimen and Site conditions.

The cutting of the root ball shall be done manually or by means of a chain 
trenching machine or mechanical tree spade. The cut will be 150 mm longer on 
each side to allow all the damaged roots to be trimmed and sealed.  Under no 
circumstances shall the initial cutting of the root ball perimeter be done with a 
backhoe or excavator. Any Palms dug in this manner will be rejected.  
3)  
Undercut the root ball horizontally by hand sufficient to enable lifting.  
563.5.13 Lifting and Transporting or Planting of Trees/Palms 
1) 
The root ball shall be thoroughly watered before lifting is carried out.  
The entire Tree shall be watered to prevent dehydration during the entire 
transport operation. 
2) 
Use only nylon "endless slings" or canvas slings for lifting. Trees with 
disfiguration from chain or rope damage will rejected or require an extended 
warranty period depending on the severity of the damage as determined by the 
Engineer. 
3) 
The root ball of tree shall be wrapped with sufficient material to minimize bare 
rooting and ensure secure packing of the roots during lifting. The lifting method 
proposed shall be submitted in writing for approval by the Engineer. 
4) 
The lifting of the Tree/Palm shall be done by means of a crane. 
5)  
Transport the Trees to the temporary Site Nursery. 
563.5.14 Tree Planting: Preliminary  
1) 
All large trees, as identified by the Engineer, shall be planted in planting holes 
lined with filter cloth. 
2) 
Planting holes shall be excavated to dimensions dictated by root ball 
dimensions. Holes shall be irregular in shape and large enough to allow a 
minimum of 300mm of backfill beneath and round the root ball. 
3) 
Line tree planting hole with filter cloth in accordance with instructions.  
Lap joints 100 minimum and return up side of planting hole. Securely peg filter 
cloth around the edges of planting hole. 
4) 
Place tree topsoil mix. Do not disturb filter cloth during placement of mix.  
Install trees as specified. 
563.5.15 Planting Operations  
1) 
Palms, Trees, Bamboo and other Plants shall be planted immediately after 
digging and transportation.

Planting holes shall be excavated to dimensions dictated by the root ball 
dimensions. Holes should be irregular in shape and large enough to allow a 
minimum of 399mm of backfill mix beneath and around the root ball. 
563.5.16 Watering 
Before planting begins, thoroughly water the root ball and planting holes.  
Water the plants immediately after planting, and thereafter as required to maintain 
growth rates free of stress. 
563.5.17 Setting Palms/Trees 
1) 
Palms/Trees shall be centered and set on compacted backfill mix that has been 
puddled and settled. 
Ensure that all palms/trees are set to their natural growing levels flush with the 
surrounding soil levels. 
2) 
Use backfill mix as specified to backfill. Set plant plumb and brace rigidly in 
position until backfill mix has been tamped solidly around root ball. When 
backfilled within 150mm of finish grade, water thoroughly, saturating root ball 
and evenly distribute planting tablets per manufacturer's instructions. Continue 
filling pit to finish grade with backfill mix. Saturate the backfill by hand 
watering during planting to expel any remaining air pockets. Form saucer berm 
around base of tree to retain water. 
563.5.18 Hormone Treatment 
Apply root including hormone to root ball surface per manufacturer's instructions. 
Guying: Immediately after planting, guy all trees as shown on details if support is 
required. 
Tree roots underground support system and Surface water collection drain system 
shall be installed in strict accordance with the approved manufacturer’s installation 
instructions. 
563.5.19 Planting Maintenance  
1) 
Maintain all Trees, Palms, Bamboo and other Plants in optimum growing 
condition and appearance.  
2) 
Maintenance as specified below shall coincide with the delivery of the first 
transplanted materials to the Site nursery and shall continue to the completion 
of the Contract and the Taking Over Certificate is issued. 
a) Irrigate all plants as required to ensure active growth keeping area moist 
but not saturated. Regulate irrigations as necessary to avoid erosion and 
gullying. 
b) Apply maintenance period fertilizer in accordance with the manufacture’s 
recommendations and the maintenance schedule.  
c) Exercise proper caution and take measures necessary to avoid plant burn.

g) Inspect all plants for disease or insect damage weekly. Treat affected

h) Remove damaged or diseased growth from Palms and Trees.

The Work 
The works in this section shall consist of the manufacture/ supply, delivery and 
installation onsite of voltage insulation and waterproofing membrane system, 
including all anchorage provisions, in accordance with this Specification and in 
conformity with the Drawings or as established by the Engineer. 
565.1.1 
General 
This method statement describes the application of voltage insulation and 
waterproofing membrane system to the surface of designated area on the platform 
station. 
After the application of voltage isolation and waterproofing membrane system, there 
shall be an insulation test performing on the voltage isolation against any leakage to 
the concrete floor. There will be two insulation test all together. The first test will be 
pre-platform floor finish, which is immediately after voltage insulation and

title: Preparation of work
text:
565.3.2 
Preparation of work 
1) Preparation of Level 
1.1) 
Study the construction drawings and identify the location of the platform 
area where the TVMS is to be installed. 
1.2) 
To determine the installation of the Platform Screen Door (PSD), it must 
first be completed before proceeding to the installation of the TVMS. A 
gap of ± 10-15mm must be maintained between the screed floor and PSD 
mounting plates to avoid direct contact between calcium silicate board 
and PSD base plates. 
1.3) 
To determine the screed floor where the TVMS is laid, it shall have a 
minimum steel troweled finish and shall be inspected prior to the 
installation by a TVMS specialist. 
1.4) 
Ensure that no sharp points or other irregularities exist, which may 
puncture the membrane system. All pipe penetration, anchor bolts for 
wall mount cladding within the surface to be insulated shall be 
preinstalled. 
1.5) 
Ensure the surface must be dry, clean, and free from sand, mud, honey 
comb, grease, oil stain, concrete droppings, cement slurry, potholes, and 
standing water. Wall where the membrane turn up shall be, should be 
plastered smoothly with non-shrink grout. 
1.6) 
WPC to provide datum line for control level. 
1.7) 
Coordinate with the APG Installer, M&E Contractor and other works of 
contractors based on the approved CSD and SEM in order to obtain 
clearance on the completion of the APG base plate or bracket prior to the 
commencement of the TVMS applications. 
2) Application of TVM System 
2.1) 
The calcium silicate board of 10mm thickness and approximately 50mm 
height shall be installed at the ±10-15mm gap in between the screed 
floor and APG transom board. The calcium silicate board shall be 
secured to the side of the screed floor by maxbond sealant. 
2.2) 
The screed floor is first primed with bituminous primer at the minimum 
of 0.3 kg per meter square. The primer is allowed to cure so that all 
inherent solvents in the primer have evaporated. Working area shall be 
barricaded to prevent unauthorized access and damage to the primer. 
2.3) 
Asphalt compound is boiled by putting the asphalt compound into a steel 
barrel, place it on top of a conventional stove and fired

by LPG gas until 
it becomes liquid. 
2.4) 
Hot bituminous asphalt trowel on the primed floor and Touch Voltage 
Membrane should then be installed simultaneously. Lapping of the 
membrane should be 10mm, which can be achieved by drawing lines on 
every rolls of the insulation membrane. 
2.5) 
Final process shall be the last layer of hot liquid asphalt wherein it is 
poured over the insulation membrane system. The touch voltage

title: Testing Procedures
text:

No other drying process is needed. 
2.6) 
Once the TVMS is fully cured, 1st insulation test shall be carried out. 
Once the testing is done, protection screed installation is to be carried out 
and followed by the installation of the finish floor and tiling of which 
these works shall be by others except for the insulation test. 
2.7) 
Installation of TVMS at the back of the house (BOH) for a measurement 
of 1.8m distance from the Platform End Door and 1.8m distance from 
the edge of the platform where the TVMS is to be installed upturn in 
order to insulate the platform edge. 
2.8) 
Hand railing located within the protection zone shall be insulated using 
UHMWPE or nylon pipe sleeve. (Where applicable). 
2.9) 
Upon completion of tiling works or floor finish, 2nd insulation test shall 
be carried out. 
3) Application Procedure of High Resistivity Sealant 
3.1) 
Sealant is applied to the gap at 1.8m from transom board of APGs and the 
gap around protection zone. This shall be done when all the floor finish 
are completed. The gap shall be clean and all loose cement stain shall be 
removed. Becker rods are placed in the gap to fill up the bottom part of 
the gap. Sealant is then applied to the top of the backer rod to fill up the 
gap and should flush with the finish floor. The completed areas shall be 
barricaded to prevent anyone from stepping over it. 
565.3.3 
Testing Procedures 
1) Upon completion of the installation works, the whole Touch Voltage Membrane 
System shall be tested in accordance to BS 62305 and BS 7430 – Code of 
Practice for Protective Earthing of Electrical Installation and any other test 
deemed necessary. 
2) The insulation test shall comply with Practice Note: Touch Voltage Membrane 
Protection for Elevated Station Platform and to be conducted in both conditions; 
dry and wet. The insulation test shall be conducted in two stages: 
2.1) 
Stage 1 – Pre-platform floor finish 
2.1.1) The measurement shall be taken when the platform or BOH is 
completed with TVMS laid. The TVMS must be clean and dry. 
The insulation test will be conducted in front of all APG doors. 
For

BOH, the test shall be conducted at one location only. 
2.1.2) Types of measurements to be conducted are: 
· Point to ground (dry condition) 
· Point to ground (wet condition) 
2.2) 
Stage 2 –Post platform finish 
2.2.1) The measurement shall be taken when the platform or BOH is 
completed with TVMS laid on floor finish. The test shall be in

2.3) 
Measurement shall be carried out as follows: 
2.3.1) Apply the prescribe voltage of 250V DC over a 300mm x 300mm

2.3.2) Repeat the procedures with wet cloth under the copper plate for

The minimum platform floor to earth resistance in dry condition shall be

The minimum platform floor to earth resistance in wet condition shall be 
10,000 ohms (0.01MΩ). 
2) Passing criteria shall be in accordance to Practice Note.

MECHANICAL GENERAL REQUIREMENTS

The Work 
The works in this section shall include the furnishing and installation of all items, 
including every article, device or accessory (whether or not specifically called for by 
item) reasonably necessary to facilitate each system's functionality as indicated by the 
design and the equipment specified. The Elements of the Work include, but are not 
limited to materials, labor, supervision, supplies, equipment, transportation, storage, 
utilities, testing and commissioning and all required permits, licenses, fees and 
royalties.

products and material requirements, testing and commissioning. However, the 
Contractor must see to it that ALL the standards below shall be in conformance with 
applicable Philippine Standards and Japan Industrial Standards (JIS) and/or equivalent 
standards. 
All materials shall be in compliance with Philippine standards and/or Japan Industry 
Standard and/or equivalent.

National Building Code of the Philippines (NBCP)  
2) 
Japanese Industrial Standards (JIS)

Guarantee  
The Contractor shall submit a single guarantee stating that the Work is in accordance 
with the contract documents. The Contractor shall be obliged to perform a Guarantee 
Work against faulty and improper and or inferior material and workmanship for a 
period of one year from the date of issue of the Certificate of Project Completion, 
except that where guarantees or warranties for longer terms are provided or specified 
herein, the longer term shall apply. The Contractor shall correct any deficiencies that 
occur during the guarantee period, within 24 hours of notification, without additional 
cost to the Employer and to the satisfaction of the Employer. The Contractor shall 
obtain similar guarantees from subcontractors, manufacturers, suppliers and sub-trade 
specialists.

Substitution 
The contract documents are based on equipment manufacturers as called out in the 
Specifications and indicated on the Drawings. Acceptance of substitute equipment 
manufacturers does not relieve the Contractor of the responsibility to provide 
equipment and materials that meet the performance as stated or implied in the contract 
documents. The Contractor shall submit proposals in writing in case he wants to make 
substitution in any materials or equipment. Said proposal shall be submitted in advance 
prior to ordering of materials or equipment to give sufficient time for the Engineer to 
review and evaluate to be with sufficient time for review prior to the date equipment 
must be ordered to maintain project schedule. Any variation for such changes or 
substitution, the Contractor shall seek approval from Employer/Engineer for costs 
associated with the review of the proposed substitution whether substitution is accepted 
or rejected. 
The Contractor shall indicate revisions required to adapt substitutions including 
revisions by other trades. Substitutions that increase the cost of the work and related 
trades are not permitted.

 Right of Way  
1) 
Pipework which pitches has the right-of-way over that which does not pitch. For 
example: condensate, steam, and plumbing drains normally have right-of-way. 
Pipework whose elevations cannot be changed have right-of-way over pipework 
whose elevations can be changed. 
2) 
Provide offsets, transitions and changes in direction of pipework, ductwork as 
required to maintain proper head room and pitch on the sloping lines. 
3) 
In cases of doubt as to the work intended, or in the event of need for explanation, 
request supplementary instructions from the Engineer. 
 Examination of Site 
1) 
Prior to the submitting of bids, visit the project site and become familiar with all 
conditions affecting the proposed installation and make provisions as to the cost 
thereof. 
2) 
The contract documents do not make representations regarding the character or 
extent of the sub-soils, water levels, existing structural, mechanical and electrical 
installations, above or below ground, or other sub-surface conditions which may 
be encountered during the work. Evaluate existing conditions, which may affect 
methods or cost of performing the work, based on examination of the site for 
other information. Failure to examine the Drawings or other information does not 
relieve the Contractor of responsibility for satisfactory completion of the work. 
 Excavation and Backfill 
1) 
Excavate all material encountered, to the depths indicated on the Drawings or as 
required. Remove from the site excavated materials not required or suitable for 
backfill. Provide grading as may be necessary to prevent surface water from 
flowing into trenches or other excavations. Remove any water which accumulates. 
Provide sheeting and shoring as may be necessary for the protection of the work 
and for the safety of personnel. 
2) 
Provide trenches of widths necessary for the proper execution of the work. Grade 
bottom of the trenches accurately to provide uniform bearing and support the 
work on undisturbed soil at every point along its en

tire length. Except where rock 
is encountered, do not excavate below the depths indicated. Where rock 
excavations are required, excavate rock to a minimum over depth of 150mm 
below the trench depths indicated on the Drawings or required. Back fill over 
depths in the rock excavation and unauthorized over depths with loose, granular, 
moist earth, thoroughly machine tamped to a compaction level of at least 95% to 
standard proctor density or 75% relative density or as specified by the Engineer. 
Whenever unstable soil that is incapable of properly supporting the work is 
encountered in the bottom of the trench, remove soil to a depth required and 
backfill the trench to the proper grade with coarse sand, fine gravel or other 
suitable materials.

The Work 
The following work shall be accomplished by the manufacturer's service 
representative or a qualified millwright or machinist approved by the Engineer: 
1) 
Pumps and Motors shall be leveled and aligned on bases and foundation pads 
in strict with the manufacturer's instructions and recommended tolerances. 
This shall be done before any piping or electrical connections are made. After 
all have been made and just prior to placing each pump in operation, levels 
and alignment shall be rechecked. All necessary adjustments shall be made to 
assure that the thrust is balanced, that shaft rotates freely when turned by hand, 
and that pump is quiet in operation. When all adjustments are completed, 
motor and pump shall be tightly bolted and grouted. 
2) 
Refrigeration Units, motors and condensers and associated eliminator pads 
shall be leveled and aligned on bases and foundation pads in strict accordance 
with the manufacturer's recommendation of tolerances and under supervision 
of the manufacturer's representative. 
All tolerances shall be checked hot and cold. A complete list of checked-out 
tolerances shall be submitted to the Engineer for review and record.

3) 
Fan and Motor Pulleys shall be carefully aligned and belt tension shall be 
properly adjusted in accordance with manufacturer's instructions. 
4) 
Centrifugal chillers, cooling towers, heat exchangers, air handling units and 
fan coil units shall be leveled and aligned on bases and foundation pads in 
strict accordance with the manufacturer's recommendation of tolerances and 
under supervision of the manufacturer's representative.

Operation 
Pumps with mechanical seals shall not be electrically operated for testing purposes 
until systems are filled with water. Seals damaged during set-up and testing shall be 
replaced at the Contractor's sole expense.

Belt and Coupling Guards 
Guards shall be provided for all belt-driven units and at chains, gears, couplings, 
keys, projecting set screws, and other rotating or moving parts. Belt guards shall be 
made to enclose both pulleys and belts on exposed sides and shall be constructed of 
galvanized steel top and bottom with expanded metal from Pittsburgh locked into 
rim. The entire assembly shall be rigidly supported with all necessary 
supplementary steel and shall be prime coated. Properly designed access openings 
shall be provided for greasing, oiling, adjusting, checking of equipment RPM, etc. 
Provide coupling guards on direct-connected units. Guards shall be designed for 
easy removal for service and shall comply with the Local Safety regulations or JIS 
Safety Requirements.

The works of this section includes all Engineering labor, materials, equipment and

System Description 
The variable capacity, heat pump heat recovery air conditioning system shall be a 
(Variable Refrigerant Flow) zoning system.  
The system shall consist of outdoor unit, multiple indoor units, and M-NET DDC 
(Direct Digital Controls). The sum of connected capacity of all indoor air handlers 
shall range from 50% to 130% of outdoor rated capacity.   
The outdoor unit shall be a horizontal discharge, 208/230volt, single-phase unit. 
Each MULTI indoor unit or group of MULTI indoor units shall be independently 
controlled.

Delivery, Storage and Handling 
Unit shall be stored and handled according to the manufacturer’s recommendation.

Controls 
1) 
The control system shall consist of a low voltage communication network of 
unitary built-in controllers with on-board communications and a web-based 
operator interface. A web controller with a network interface card shall gather 
data from this system and generate web pages accessible through a 
conventional web browser on each PC connected to the network. Operators 
shall be able to perform all normal operator functions through the web 
browser interface. 
2) 
System controls and control components shall be installed in accordance with 
the manufacturer’s written installation instructions. 
3) 
Furnish energy conservation features such as optimal start, night setback, 
request-based logic, and demand level adjustment of overall system capacity 
as specified in the sequence.  
4) 
System shall provide direct and reverse-acting on and off algorithms based on 
an input condition or group conditions to cycle a binary output or multiple 
binary outputs. 
5) 
Provide capability for future system expansion to include monitoring and use 
of occupant card access, lighting control and general equipment control. 
6) 
System shall be capable of email generation for remote alarm annunciation.  
7) 
Control system start-up shall be a required service to be completed by the 
manufacturer or a duly authorized, competent representative that has been 
factory trained in Heat Reclaim Ventilation (HRV) manufacturer’s controls 
system configuration and operation. The representative shall provide proof of

For climates that experience snowfall, mount the outdoor unit a minimum of 12”

 Components / Piping 
Installing contractor shall provide and install all accessories and piping for a fully 
operational system. Refer to manufacturer’s installation manual for full instructions.    
Traps, filter driers, and sight glasses are NOT to be installed on the refrigerant 
piping or condensate lines. 
Standard ACR fittings rated for use with R410A are to be used for all connections. 
Proprietary manufacturer-specific appurtenances are not allowed.   
Refrigerant pipe for HRV shall be made of phosphorus deoxidized copper, and has 
two types.  
1) 
ACR “Annealed”: Soft copper pipe, can be easily bent with human's hand.  
2) 
ACR “Drawn Temper”: Hard copper pipe (Straight pipe), being stronger than 
Type-O pipe of the same radical thickness.  
The maximum operation pressure of R410A air conditioner is 4.30 MPa [623psi]. 
The refrigerant piping should ensure the safety under the maximum operation 
pressure. Refer to recommend piping specifications in Mitsubishi Electric’s 
engineering manual. Pipes of radical thickness 0.7mm or less shall not be used.  
Flare connection should follow dimensions provided in manufacturer’s installation 
manuals.  
 Insulation

cell pipe insulation for piping up to 1”in diameter, or ¾” for piping 1-1/8” and larger, 
with a thermal conductivity no greater than 0.27 BTU-in/hr sq.ft oF.  If state or local 
codes require insulation other than that specified above, the greater insulation shall 
be used.

Inertia Blocks 
Inertia blocks shall be factory fabricated, and shall consist of a structural steel 
channel or I-beam perimeter frame with brackets for each isolation support, with 
adequate steel reinforcing to prevent flexure due to equipment operating forces and 
with height saving brackets welded to the frame. Height of the frame shall be as 
required to provide the thickness or weight as indicated or hereinafter specified, and 
shall not be less than 1/12 of the length of the frame. Templates for equipment bolt 
holes and/or fastenings shall be provided. Concrete for inertia blocks shall be 
poured on roofing paper within the structural perimeter frame. Concrete shall be in 
accordance with the requirements of Section 405, Concrete Structures.

Spring Isolators 
Spring isolators shall be designed and installed so that the ends of the spring are 
constructed to remain parallel during deflection and shall be provided with leveling 
bolts. Isolators shall be positioned in accordance with the weight distribution to 
ensure adequate deflection and vibration isolation. Housing or snubbing devices 
shall not be used to contain the isolation springs unless specified. To achieve 
stability the ratio of the spring diameter to compressed height of each spring shall 
not be less than 0.8, and springs shall have a minimum of 50% additional travel to 
solid beyond rated deflection. Springs shall be so designed that the ratio of 
horizontal spring constant to vertical spring constant is between one and two. If the 
mounting base plate is bolted to the floor, vibration isolation washers and grommets 
shall be used between the nuts and bolts and the isolator to prevent short-circuiting. 
1) 
Free Standing Spring Isolators 
Isolators shall be free standing, open spring type with levelling bolts and 
mounting base. Each spring mounting shall have a minimum 6.5mm thick 
ribbed neoprene pad adhered to underside of base. 
2) 
Vertically-Restrained Spring Isolators 
Isolators shall be open spring type designed to provide adjustable vertical 
restraint, with suitable neoprene grommets on restraining rod to prevent 
"Shorting". Diameters shall be as hereinbefore specified for Spring Isolators. 
3) 
Vibration Rail Bases 
Bases shall be structural steel members arranged to form a rigid support, with 
mounting provisions for neoprene or spring mountings, and height saving 
welded-on steel isolator brackets. Height of steel shall be not less than 1/10 of 
the length of the base.

Integral Steel Fan and Motor Bases 
Bases shall be structural steel, welded and reinforced as necessary to prevent flexure 
of the base. Height of steel shall be not less than 1/10 of the length of the base. The 
structural base for the fan and motor shall be continuous and integral. Motor slide

General 
The Specification and Drawings indicate the extent and general arrangement of the 
piping system. If any departure from the drawings are deemed necessary by the

shall be submitted to the Engineer for approval. 
All pipework shall be constructed of new pipes and accessories conforming to the

specified and/or shown on the Drawings.

Cross-Connections and Interconnections 
No Plumbing fixtures, special equipment, device, or piping, shall be installed which 
will provide cross-connection or interconnection between a distributing supply for 
drinking water or domestic water and a polluted supply or waste such as a drainage 
system or a soil or waste pipe so as to make possible the backflow or back siphonage 
of sewage or polluted water into the potable water supply system. Where the 
possibility of back-siphonage exists, water supplied to the fixture shall be 
introduced through a suitable vacuum breaker installed at minimum of 2.3m above 
the floor. Make up water for cooling towers shall be supplied through a cistern tank 
in order to prevent cross-connection.

Layout 
Give careful consideration to clearance under beams, over windows, etc. to provide 
maximum headroom in all cases and to the locations of lines and type of fittings 
used to obtain these clearances. Ascertain from the drawings the heights of all 
suspended ceilings and the size of all pipe shafts in which piping is to be concealed, 
and the location and size of structural members in and adjacent to all pipe shafts. In 
any case where insufficient room is provided for piping above suspended ceilings

Booster Pump Assembly, Inverter Type 
 2-Pump Unit Type 
1) 
The assembly shall be of variable flow constant pressure booster system.

The unit shall consist of four (2) pumps, pressure tank, control panel and all

3) 
Operation method: 
a) A unit shall have the same two pumps but named lead pump and 
support/stand-by pump. Each pump is cyclically changed when a unit is 
stopped. 
b) When water is required the lead pump starts, and when no water is required 
lead pump stops. But when water is required more that can be provided by the 
lead pump operation, the support pump starts and a unit shifts to parallel 
operation of the two pumps. As less water is required the support pump and 
the lead pump stop in sequence. In the event of trouble occurring to one pump, 
the other pump will operate in parallel alternate operation. 
4) 
Control method: 
Lead pump starts: Pressure switch for lead pump

- ON 
Support pump starts: Pressure switch for support pump

- ON 
Support pump stops: Pressure switch for support pump

- OFF 
Lead pump stops: Both pressure switch and flow switch for lead pump -OFF

Water Supply Piping 
 General 
Before pipes are laid, the positions where water supply pipes are connected with other 
equipment, pipes and apparatus shall be checked and the gradient of pipes shall be 
examined, then the precise location shall be decided. 
As the work progresses, hangers shall be furnished and pipe sleeves shall be concealed 
without delay. Main pipes shall have flange joints at adequate points. The pipes which 
are exposed to view and not more than 25mm in nominal diameter shall be allowed to be 
jointed into union joints. 
At the branches tees shall be used. 
The pipe section, in which air or mud is likely to stay, shall be equipped with an air vent 
or a mud ejection valve. Where the nominal diameter of water supply pipe is not greater 
than 25mm, the mud ejection valve shall be of the same diameter. However, where the 
nominal diameter of water supply pipe is greater than 25mm, the diameter of mud 
ejection valve shall be 25mm. 
As to indoor piping which is not protected by anti-sweat covering, the portion where the 
pipe penetrates the ceiling, floor or wall, etc., shall be provided with washers. The part 
where concealed main pipe branches off or makes a bend shall be, wherever required, 
protected with concrete, etc. from impact.

Steel pipes where concealed underground shall be taped with anti-corrosive vinyl tape. 
Lead pipe where concealed in concrete shall be wrapped with waterproof flax and then

 Gradient 
In case of riser type piping, horizontal pipe shall have an upward gradient. In case of drip 
riser type piping, horizontal pipes shall have a downward gradient. In both cases, the 
gradient shall be more than 1/250.

Installation of Water Pipes 
The piping shall be extended to all fixture, outlets, and equipment from the gate valves 
installed in the branch near the riser. 
The water system shall be installed with a fall toward a main shut-off valve and drains. 
Ends of pipes and outlets shall be capped or plugged and left ready for future connection. 
 Mains and Branches 
1) 
All pipes shall be accurately cut to measurements and shall be worked into place 
without springing or forcing. Care shall be taken so as not to weaken the structural 
portions of the building. 
2) 
All piping above the ground shall run parallel with the lines of the building unless 
otherwise shown on the Drawings.  
3) 
All service pipes, valves and fitting shall be kept at sufficient distance from other 
work to permit finished covering not less than one half inch from such other work 
or from finished covering different service. 
4) 
No water piping shall be buried in floor unless specifically indicated on the 
Drawings or approved by the Engineer. 
5) 
Changes in pipes sizes be made with reducing fittings. 
6) 
All joint shall be tested at 100 psi for two hours before covering. 
 Thread Pipe Joint 
1) 
All pipes shall be reamed before threading. All screw joint shall be made with 
graphite compound to male threads only. Threads shall be cut and not more than 
three threads on the pipe shall remain exposed. 
2) 
Caulking of threaded joints to stop or prevent leaks shall not be required for 
disconnection.

Disinfection 
The entire system shall be thoroughly flushed and disinfected with chlorine before it is 
placed in operation. Chlorinating material shall be liquid chlorine or hypochlorite and 
shall be introduced into the waterline in a manner approved by the Engineer. 
The chlorine dosage shall be such as to provide no less than 50ppm of available chlorine. 
Following a contact period of not less than 16 hours, the heavily chlorinated water shall 
be flushed from the system until the residual chlorine content is no greater than two tents 
ppm.

The Work 
The works of this section covered the specifications includes all labor, materials, 
equipment, services, facilities and all items necessary to complete testing, inspections 
and commissioning of geothermal cooling system.

Outline of the System 
The geothermal cooling system shall consist of the following facilities: 
a)  
Ground loop piping facilities 
b)  
Water-water heat exchanger facilities 
c)  
Indoor cooling facilities

Description of Facilities 
 Ground Loop Piping Facilities 
Ground loop piping facilities consist of the vertical ground heat exchangers in bore holes, 
the horizontal closed loop piping, the flow meter and the pipe-insertion-type 
thermometers. The chilled water on the heat source side will circulate through the vertical 
ground heat exchangers and the horizontal closed loop piping, and the heat will be 
removed from the chilled water as the ground beneath the ground level is cooler all the 
year. Bore holes will be at least one hundred meters long and the number of bore holes is 
determined according to the required cooling capacity and the removed heat capacity per 
meter of a bore hole. 
The chilled water removed heat will then flow to the water-water heat exchanger. 
 Water-water Heat Exchanger Facilities 
Water-water heat exchanger is used for heat exchange between the chilled water on the 
heat source side (bore hole side) and the chilled water on the indoor cooling equipment 
side. The primary pumps, the secondary pumps, the expansion tanks and headers are 
included in the water-water heat exchanger facilities. The primary pumps have the 
necessary capability to circulate the chilled water on the heat source side through the bore 
holes. The secondary pumps have the necessary capability to circulate the chilled water 
on the indoor cooling equipment side through the chilled water closed loop piping. 
 Indoor Cooling Facilities 
Indoor cooling facilities consist of indoor cooling equipment such as fan coil units, the 
closed loop piping, the flow meter and the pipe-insertion-type thermometers. The chilled 
water on the indoor cooling equipment side will circulate through the chilled water closed 
loop piping and remove the heat from the indoor space with the cooling equipment. The 
chilled water which removes the heat in the indoor space will enter again to the water-
water heat exchanger and emit the heat to the chilled water on the heat source side.

 Quantity of Heat per meter of a Bore Hole 
Approximately 40 to 70 watt/meter 
The quantity of heat per meter of a bore hole depends on the thermal characteristics of 
the ground formation and the existence of the ground water on the site. The ground 
formation survey and the thermal response test shall be implemented prior to the detailed 
design of the geothermal cooling system. 
 Heat Transfer Fluid 
The heat transfer fluid shall be propylene glycol 30% solution (by weight). 
 Specification of Ground Heat Exchangers 
The ground heat exchanger shall consist of the double U-tubes of 25mm in diameter 
which are at least one hundred meters long. The U-tubes shall be made of high density 
polyethylene (PE100 in accordance with ISO/TR9080) and SDR (Standard Dimension 
Ratio: the diameter of the outer pipe divided by the thickness of the pipe) shall be equal 
to or less than 11, as the high long-term hydrostatic pressure strength and the long life is 
required for the ground closed loop piping, as well as the impact resistance and the 
moderate flexibility. In addition, the U-tubes shall meet the heat static performance and 
the strength against creep by the inner pressure, in accordance with the requirement for 
“Polyethylene double layer pipe for portable water supply” (JIS K 6762).  
The ground heat exchange shall be installed in a bore hole of at least 150mm in diameter. 
Bore holes shall be excavated at intervals of at least four meters.  
 Specification of Horizontal Closed Loop Piping 
The pipes and fittings which consist of the same materials as the ground heat exchangers 
shall be used for the horizontal closed loop piping. The joint fittings of the embedded 
piping shall be electrofusion joints.  
The exposed piping in indoor spaces or outdoors shall be insulated in accordance with 
610 PIPING INSULATION of this technical specification, or local technical codes, 
whichever is more stringent.

about 200mm below the surface.

and pull-boxes shall be located to avoid interference with foundations, 
piping and other similar underground work.

accomplished by long sweep bends having a minimum radius of curvature

Excavation and Back Fill 
1) 
Provide excavation for the work of this section. Excavate all material 
encountered, to the depths indicated on the drawings or as required. Remove 
from the site excavated materials NOT required or suitable for backfill. 
Provide grading as may be necessary to prevent surface water from flowing 
into trenches or other excavations. Remove any water which accumulates. 
Provide sheeting and shoring as may be necessary for the protection of the 
work and safety of personnel. 
2) 
Provide trenches of widths necessary for the proper execution of the work. 
Grade bottom of the trenches accurately to provide uniform bearing and 
support the work on undisturbed soil at every point along its entire length. 
Except where rock is encountered, do not excavate below the depths indicated. 
Where rock excavations are required, excavate rock to a minimum over depth 
of four inches below the trench depths indicated on the Drawings or required. 
Backfill over depths in the rock excavation and unauthorized over depths with 
loose, granular, moist earth, thoroughly machine tamped to a compaction 
level of at least 95% to standard proctor density or 75% relative density or as 
specified by the architect. Wherever unstable soil that is incapable of properly 
supporting the work is encountered in the bottom of the trench, remove soil 
to a depth required and backfill the trench to the proper grade with coarse sand, 
fine gravel or other suitable material. 
3)

of cover from existing grade or from indicated finished grade, whichever is 
lower, unless otherwise specifically shown.

b) Telephone service: 70cm minimum

System Overview 
 Automatic Fire Alarm 
The automatic fire alarm, whose function chart is shown below, automatically 
detects smoke or heat from a fire with the help of detectors and indicates the location 
of the fire to the receiver (multiple control panel). A person who has detected a fire 
may operate the manual call button to inform the receiver of the location of the fire. 
The receiver, in turn, displays the location where the fire has broken out and made 
a distinct sound throughout the building. 
 Smoke Fire Damper Control (SFD Control) 
The smoke fire damper control which is configured as shown below, causes the 
interlock control panel to receive a signal from the automatic fire alarm's smoke 
detector by way of the fire alarm receiver and closes the smoke fire damper (SFD; 
see the SFD closure matrix table) associated with the location of a fire. The interlock 
control panel displays the location of the SFD which has operated and also sends 
an associated air conditioner stop signal to the air conditioner control panel. This 
signal is sent to the CPU of the control center to stop the air-conditioner and the fan.

Uninterruptible Power Supply (UPS) 
UPS shall be provided to supply continuous electrical power for BMS 
An UPS shall be sized to power its full connected load for two hours.  
The UPS shall include a rectifier/charger section, inverter section, a static by-pass 
switch, a manual by-pass switch, battery and all necessary control. 
The UPS shall be provided in a single cabinet complete with control switches and 
meter. Its audible noise level shall not exceed 55 dBA at 1.5m in the front panel, 
over a load range 10% to 100% full load. 
The battery shall consist of sealed lead-acid cells, thus obviating the specific need 
for flameproof equipment in the Station Office. These shall be mounted in at least 
one cabinet.  
The inverter shall provide a 3 phase 400/230 V, 60Hz output, stabilized to 5% from 
on-load to full load, with batteries from 100% to 20% charged.

The Work 
The works in this section shall furnish, install, and place in operating condition an 
electrically supervised, surveillance system as described herein. The system shall 
include the CCTV cameras, CCTV monitors, Pan/Tilt/Motorized Zoom Lens 
mechanisms and remote control units, multiplexer, video recorder, indoor housings, 
wires and cables, conduits, power supplies, fittings and accessories required to 
provide a complete operating system.

Type of System 
The CCTV/Surveillance system shall operate as a completely supervised Closed 
Circuit Television System integrated to Building Management System (BMS)

System Operation 
The surveillance system shall consist of CCTV cameras combination of fixed and 
equipped with Pan/Tilt/Zoom Lens System (PTZ) located at the lobbies and 
entrances and exits of Ground and Second floors. CCTV monitors and remote 
control units shall be located at the Security Room. A master controller shall be 
provided wherein a CCTV video monitor and video tape recorder shall be connected 
to record the display of a preselected camera view. Video inputs to the multiplexer 
and sequential switcher shall come from the video outputs of CCTV cameras. The 
master controller shall function as a bridging auto alarming switch. 
Under normal condition, the operator has the option to either manually or 
automatically sequence the cameras. The CCTV cameras can be viewed on the 
monitors using multiplexer and sequential switchers. 
When an alarm occurs, the auto alarming sequence goes into effect. The video 
signal from the camera covering the alarmed area is displayed on monitor, an 
audible signal notifies the operator of an alarm, a video tape recorder is 
automatically switched on to record the video from the second monitor and a LED 
illuminates the “confirm alarm” button until acknowledged by the operator. Should 
multiple alarms occur, each is automatically sequenced until confirmed by the 
operator.

Management Software 
a) The management software shall allow control and monitor of access and 
security to the proposed facility and remote facilities. The software shall 
allow centralized alarming, card holder management etc. and shall have

b) The management system shall use Employer Server architecture bases

managed by the system servers. 
h) A download of newly entered card or cardholder information shall 
automatically be initiated on each remote system server when manually 
initiated on any local system server. Such downloads may in0clude 
multiple sets of cards or cardholders.

Zones

Description

Security 
Managing cardholders shall only be available to operators who are at a certain 
security level. Both cardholders and cards shall also confirm to standard system 
Operator Security features such as area assignment as defined in this section.  
It shall be possible to define an operator as only a cardholder administrator. All 
other functions in the system will be restricted to this operator except for cardholder 
administration functions.

Assigning Access to Cardholders 
Cardholders may have up to 8 different access levels assigned to them. Each of 
these access levels may define a separate set of readers and times that will allow the 
cardholder access. Operators shall be presented with a list of all access levels 
already assigned to the cardholder and all access levels that are currently unassigned.

Deleting Cardholders 
Cardholders may be deleted but retained in the database for future reference if 
required. It shall then be possible to "undelete" the cardholder should this be 
required. It shall also be possible to permanently delete the cardholder record in 
order to prevent unnecessarily large databases from developing.

Card/ Cardholder Expiry 
Cardholder and card expiry dates may be defined down to a resolution of date and 
time in minutes.  
It shall be possible to assign cardholders and cards separate expiry dates, enabling 
a card assigned to a cardholder to expire before the cardholder expires. However, it 
shall not be possible for the card expiry date to exceed the cardholder expiry date 
of the cardholder to which a card is assigned.  
Expiry dates may be set up by default to be a particular given date, or a relative 
period from the time the cardholder was created (e.g. 1 year).  
 Cardholder alarms 
It shall be possible to specify that the cardholder generate an alarm when they use 
their card. This setting may override the alarm setting of the reader to which a 
cardholder may be presenting their card.  
 Cardholder events 
All changes to cardholders in the system shall be logged in the event summary and 
shall list the new value of the cardholder field. Similarly, any time a cardholder 
accesses a card reader; an event will be listed in the event summary. It shall be 
possible to automatically view all the events generated for a particular cardholder 
directly from the cardholder displays without having to run a separate report.

support the proximity smart cards compliant with UL 294 Listed. It shall support 
Card plus PIN reader and Card only reader. The reader shall include beepers, and

access denied. A green LED shall flash green

for access granted and shall show 
solid green when there is free access. A method of LED indication shall be required

from that zone by presenting their card to an exit reader.

Free access - Door is unlocked, no card entry required.  
2) 
Secure access - Door is locked, a successful card attempt is required for valid

3) 
Secure + PIN access - Door is locked, a successful card and correct PIN 
number attempt is required for valid entry. Door re-secures after access 
attempt.  
4) 
Override from reader - Members of certain access groups shall be able to 
change the access and PINs mode of the door at certain times.  
5) 
Dual Authorization - access is granted only when two different but legitimate 
cards are presented within a given time frame.  
6) 
Escort – A second card is required to be presented from a cardholder who is 
nominated in the “Escort Access Group”.  
7) 
Shared PIN Number - The system Operator determines what the PIN number 
will be and programs this into the system. Access is allowed through the door 
when the correct 4 digit PIN is pressed followed by the "Enter" key.  
Cardholder access reporting to the central control and logging in the audit trail shall

Only when there has been a successful presentation of a valid access card AND the

Whenever there has been a successful presentation of a valid access card

FIRE DETECTION AND ALARM SYSTEM

The Work  
The work of this section covers the furnishing, installing and placing in operation 
of an electronically-operated, supervised, conventional fire alarm system. 
All units of equipment shall be in accordance the requirements of the PMEC for 
pull station signaling use and shall consist of control unit, manual fire boxes, alarm 
indicating appliances and automatic smoke and heat detectors, all located on the 
Drawings and wired in accordance with the manufacturer’s instructions to make a 
complete and workable system. 
System equipment and components furnished and installed under this section shall 
be fabricated, assembled, erected, and placed in proper operating condition in full 
conformity with the drawings, specifications, engineering data, instructions, and 
recommendations of the equipment manufacturer unless exceptions are noted by 
the Employer.

Performance and Design Requirements 
1) 
Design Criteria 
The operation of any manual pull station or automatic alarm initiating devices 
shall start the audible and visual location alarm indicating appliances as herein 
described. 
The audible alarm indicating devices shall sound the standard evacuation tone 
temporal pattern three, and visual alarms flash, until alarm initiating devices 
have been restored to normal and a reset switch located at the control panel 
actuated, except that audible and visual alarms may be discontinued at the 
control panel actuated, except that audible and visual alarms may be 
discontinued at the control panel as herein specified.

Components 
1) 
Automatic Fire Detectors 
Detectors shall be of the following types, selected by the Contractors for 
correct temperature and as approved by the Employer. The detectors shall be 
designed with an inherent stability that prevents false alarms caused by 
transient electrical disturbances, condensation of humidity, barometric 
pressure shall be provided. 
a) Location 
Detectors shall be installed approximately where indicated on the 
drawings and as required by PMEC and Philippine Fire Code. In no case, 
shall detectors be installed in locations that subject them to the direct air 
supply diffusers or to heat from lighting fixtures or other heat sources, in 
a manner affecting their normal operation. 
b) Spacing 
Detectors spacing on smooth surface shall not exceed distance 
recommended by the testing and approving agency for the particular 
device installed. In areas where irregularities exceed those described, the 
distance, the detectors spacing shall be reduced to provide detection 
coverage equaling or exceeding that required for smooth surfaces. An 
open area underneath a deck, mezzanine, or floor landing of a stairway 
having a minor linear dimension of 1.2 meters or more shall be considered 
a separate subdivision and protected accordingly. 
c) Ionization smoke detectors 
Ionization detectors shall operate on the ionization principle and shall be 
activated by the presence of combustion products. It shall be possible by 
electrically check and readjust the detector as required. The detector head 
shall contain an indicator lamp, which shall light to indicate the indication 
of the alarm. 
2) 
Audible and Visual Indicator

a) Visual Indicator 
Provide surface-mounted lamp assembly for use in an electrically-
supervised circuit. Provide lamps of the flashing stroboscopic 
incandescent type powered from the Control Panel Alarm Circuit. Lamps 
shall produce a minimum of 50 candlepower and flash between 60 and 
120 times per minute. Lamps shall be protected by a red thermoplastic 
lens. 
b) Alarm Horns 
Alarm horns shall be compliant with the Philippines Fire Code and be the 
combination audio-visual type rated 97 dB at a distance of 3 meters. Horns 
shall be vibrating type with stainless steel diaphragms. Vibration shall be 
generated by an electromagnetic operating at 24 volts DC. Frames and 
single projector horn shall be cast aluminum, surface mounted. Additional 
signage shall be provided in English. Horns installed outdoor shall be 
listed for outdoor use. 
Combination Audio-Visual horn/lamp units shall be installed on 
supervised circuit. Visual portion shall flash on alarm condition. 
3) 
Alarm Control Panel 
Control Panel shall contain number of zones as indicated on the Drawings. 
Unless otherwise indicated, the system controls shall be housed in a surface 
wall-mounted in NEMA 3 dust tight enclosure cabinet with an extruded 
anodized aluminum door and full viewing window. All annunciator 
indications and operating instructions shall be clearly visible through the 
viewing window. The door shall provide access to all operating controls, but 
will not expose live electrical connections and shall be furnished with lock 
and common key with other FACP’s. All electrical connections shall be front 
access through the hinged door and removable dead-front panel. Control 
circuits and protective device shall be contained behind a dead-front panel 
which requires the use of a tool to gain access. Actuation of any alarm 
initiating device shall cause all audible alarm devices to sound continuously. 
Alarm initiating devices shall be grouped into multiple zones as indicated on 
the drawings. The electrically supervised lamp indicator on the control unit 
shall indicate the zone of the fire. 
a) Construction 
The control panel shall be of modular construction. Each individual 
functions

shall be on replaceable plug-in panel or module. All plug-in 
modules and panel connectors shall be supervised as so to give trouble 
signal if removed or disconnected. All alarm initiating and alarm 
indicating circuit extending from the fire alarm control unit and shall be 
energy limited in accordance with the requirements for limited energy 
circuits. 
b) Control Unit Functions 
The control unit shall contain the following functions and modules.

The control unit shall provide one alarm-receiving module for each fire 
zone of the building protected as indicated on the drawings. The wiring 
for the alarm initiating devices up to and including the alarm relay coil 
shall be supervised against an open circuit fault condition.  Operation of 
an initiating devise shall cause an individual red supervised alarm zone to 
lock and shall provide an alarm output to other sections of the control unit. 
Circuitry and terminals shall be provided to connect additional supervised 
remote annunciation. Any fault condition on the wiring to any remote 
annunciator shall not prevent all annunciator from functioning properly 
on all zones. An individual amber trouble lamp shall be provided for each 
alarm receiving zone to indicate the location of any faults in the wiring to 
initiating devices.  Terminals shall be provided for connection of remote 
zone trouble indicators. The alarm receiving circuits shall have a class B 
operation.  A single break or ground fault in the wiring initiating devices 
shall provide a trouble signal.  
d) Lamp Supervision 
The current used to supervise lamps shall be low enough not to cause the 
lamp filaments to glow or decrease the rated life of the lamp. Failure of an 
alarm on the control unit shall cause the trouble signal to sound. 
e) Lamp Test 
The control unit alarm and trouble lamps maybe tested to locate a lamp 
failure by depressing the lamp bush button. 
f) Reset 
When the alarm initiating devices have been restored depressing the lamp 
test button shall reset the system control. 
4) 
Subsequent Alarm 
An alarm from any receiving circuit shall cause the audible signals to sound 
for a full period, whether or not a previous alarm has partially or fully time-
out by means of an automatic time limit cutout or has been silenced manually. 
Silencing by any means shall cause a red “signal silenced” lamp in the panel 
to illuminate and the trouble signal to sound.

The control unit shall provide a drill switch and drill light.  Operation of the drill
